student_will_learn: Explain the trade-offs between S3 Standard, Infrequent Access, Glacier, and Deep Archive
Explain how retrieval time and cost trade off against storage cost across storage classes
Configure a lifecycle policy to automatically transition objects between storage classes
Match a data access pattern to the correct storage class
Identify why actively-served content should never be moved to an archival storage class

ava_lesson_intro.ava_speaks: Last lesson-ல நாம S3-ஓட bucket/object model பார்த்தோம். இப்போ CFO-ஓட FQ-189 ticket-ல real கேள்வி - 'ஒரே storage class-ல எல்லாத்தையும் வெச்சிருக்கறோமா, அல்லது data-ஓட access pattern-ஐ பொறுத்து cost optimize பண்ணலாமா?' இதுதான் இன்னைக்கு நாம கத்துக்கப் போற S3 Storage Classes.

lines: Building Basics · Session CS5 · Lesson C5.1b
Ticket FQ-189 — continuing with CFO's Office

blocks.block_title: Storage Cost vs Retrieval Cost vs Retrieval Time
blocks.ava_speaks: S3-ல பல storage classes இருக்கும், ஒவ்வொண்ணும் ஒரு different trade-off offer பண்ணும். S3 Standard, அதிக storage cost, ஆனா immediate retrieval, frequent access-க்கு நல்லது. S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access), storage cost குறைவு, ஆனா ஒவ்வொரு retrieval-க்கும் ஒரு extra cost இருக்கும் - infrequently access பண்ற ஆனா immediate access தேவைப்படற data-க்கு. Glacier, storage cost ரொம்ப குறைவு, ஆனா retrieval minutes முதல் hours வரைக்கும் ஆகலாம். Deep Archive, cheapest storage, ஆனா retrieval 12+ hours ஆகலாம் - long-term compliance archives-க்கு மட்டும்.

board_actions.text: S3 Storage Classes — The Trade-off Spectrum

Cheaper storage always comes with either a retrieval fee, a retrieval delay, or both — there's no free lunch. The right class depends entirely on how often and how urgently the data needs to be accessed.

inline_questions.question: ஒரு data set, ஆண்டுக்கு ஒரு தடவை மட்டும் access பண்ணப்படும், ஆனா access பண்ணும்போது சில மணி நேரம் காத்திருக்கறது problem இல்ல (compliance archive). எந்த storage class பொருந்தும்?
options: A) S3 Standard, ஏன்னா அது fastest
B) S3 Glacier அல்லது Deep Archive, cheapest storage, retrieval delay acceptable-ஆ இருக்கறதால
C) S3 Standard-IA, ஏன்னா அது balanced
D) இது எந்த storage class-லும் store பண்ண முடியாது
inline_questions.ava_correct: Correct! Rarely accessed, delay tolerable-ஆ இருந்தா, Glacier அல்லது Deep Archive தான் cheapest option - retrieval delay இங்க ஒரு problem இல்ல.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல, S3 Standard இங்க unnecessary-ஆ expensive - ஆண்டுக்கு ஒரு தடவை மட்டும் access பண்றது, delay tolerate பண்ண முடியற data-க்கு, Glacier அல்லது Deep Archive தான் cost-effective.

inline_questions.question: Cheaper storage class தேர்ந்தெடுக்கும்போது, என்ன trade-off பண்றோம்?
options: A) எந்த trade-off-மும் இல்ல, எல்லாமே ஒரே service quality
B) Retrieval cost அதிகரிக்கும், retrieval time அதிகரிக்கும், அல்லது ரெண்டுமே
inline_questions.ava_correct: Sari! Storage cost குறைஞ்சா, retrieval fee அதிகரிக்கலாம், retrieval time (minutes to hours) அதிகரிக்கலாம், அல்லது ரெண்டுமே - இதுதான் real trade-off, durability affect ஆகாது.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல, durability எல்லா storage classes-லும் (Deep Archive உட்பட) high-ஆவே இருக்கும் - real trade-off retrieval cost மற்றும் retrieval time, storage cost குறையும்போது.

blocks.block_title: Automating the Trade-off With Lifecycle Policies
blocks.ava_speaks: ஒரு common pattern - data 'new'-ஆ இருக்கும்போது frequently access பண்ணப்படும், time போக போக access frequency குறையும். FoodQuick-ஓட old order invoices, generate ஆன முதல் 30 நாள் frequently access பண்ணப்படும் (customer support queries), அதுக்கு அப்புறம் almost ஒரு போதும் access பண்ணப்படாது, ஆனா compliance-க்காக 7 வருடம் retain பண்ணனும். Manual-ஆ ஒவ்வொரு file-ஐயும் move பண்றதுக்கு பதிலா, lifecycle policies use பண்ணி automatic transitions set பண்ணலாம். Freshworks மாதிரி companies, invoices, logs, backups எல்லாத்துக்கும் இதே pattern use பண்றாங்க - storage cost automatically optimize ஆகும், manual intervention தேவை இல்லாம.

board_actions.text: Lifecycle Policy — Automatic Cost Optimization Over Time

blocks.block_title: Setting Up a Lifecycle Policy for Order Invoices
blocks.ava_speaks: karthik-dev இப்போ FoodQuick-ஓட order invoices bucket-க்கு ஒரு lifecycle policy configure பண்றான் - automatic-ஆ storage class transition ஆக.

steps.ava_narration: S3 Console-ல foodquick-order-invoices bucket-க்கு போய், 'Management' tab-ல 'Lifecycle rules' -> 'Create lifecycle rule' click பண்றோம்.

console_action.path: S3 Console → foodquick-order-invoices → Management → Lifecycle rules → Create lifecycle rule
console_action.result: The lifecycle rule creation form opens

steps.ava_narration: Rule name 'invoice-cost-optimization' கொடுத்து, scope-ஆ 'Apply to all objects in the bucket' select பண்றோம்.

console_action.value: invoice-cost-optimization, Apply to all objects in the bucket
console_action.highlight: Rule name field and scope selector
console_action.result: The rule will apply to every invoice object in this bucket

steps.ava_narration: 'Transition current versions of objects' enable பண்றோம் - 30 நாள் கழிச்சு S3 Standard-IA-க்கு, 365 நாள் கழிச்சு Glacier Deep Archive-க்கு transition பண்ண.

console_action.value: 30 days -> S3 Standard-IA, 365 days -> Glacier Deep Archive
console_action.highlight: Transition day count and target storage class fields
console_action.result: Objects will automatically move to cheaper storage classes as they age, with no manual intervention needed

steps.ava_narration: Expiration-ஆ, 2555 நாள் (7 வருடம்) கழிச்சு object delete பண்ண set பண்றோம் - compliance retention period முடிஞ்ச பிறகு.

console_action.result: Invoices older than 7 years will be automatically and permanently deleted, matching the compliance retention requirement

steps.ava_narration: Rule review பண்ணி, 'Create rule' click பண்றோம்.

console_action.result: The lifecycle policy is now active and will run automatically going forward

expected_outcome.description: Order invoices now automatically transition from Standard to Standard-IA at 30 days, to Glacier Deep Archive at 365 days, and expire entirely after 7 years — all without any manual file management.
expected_outcome.what_to_notice: Lifecycle policy ஒரு one-time setup - இதுக்கு அப்புறம், ஒவ்வொரு புது invoice-மும் automatic-ஆ இதே rule-ஐ follow பண்ணும், manual intervention தேவை இல்ல.

blocks.block_title: An Object's Journey Through Its Lifecycle
blocks.ava_speaks: இந்த diagram பாரு - ஒரு single invoice object, time போக போக எப்படி storage classes-ஐ மாறி மாறி போகுதுனு காட்டுது.

ascii: Day 0: Invoice created -> S3 Standard (frequent access expected)
Day 30: Lifecycle rule triggers -> S3 Standard-IA (occasional access, cheaper storage)
Day 365: Lifecycle rule triggers -> S3 Glacier Deep Archive (compliance-only, cheapest storage)
Day 2555 (7 years): Lifecycle rule triggers -> Object permanently deleted
Cost per GB decreases at each transition; retrieval time increases at each transition.

output_preview.ava_narration: இந்த முழு journey-யும் automatic-ஆ நடக்கும் - யாரும் manual-ஆ track பண்ணி move பண்ண வேண்டாம்.

blocks.block_title: Your Turn — Design a Lifecycle Policy for Application Logs
blocks.instruction: FoodQuick-ஓட application logs bucket-க்கு, correct lifecycle policy design பண்ணு.
blocks.scenario: CFO-ஓட office, application logs storage cost ரொம்ப அதிகமா இருக்குனு flag பண்ணி இருக்காங்க. Logs, முதல் 7 நாள் active debugging-க்கு frequently access பண்ணப்படும், 7-90 நாள் இடையே rare debugging lookups-க்கு access பண்ணப்படும், 90 நாளுக்கு அப்புறம் almost ஒரு போதும் access பண்ணப்படாது, ஆனா audit requirements-க்காக 1 வருடம் retain பண்ணணும்.

starter_state.console_open: S3 Console → foodquick-application-logs → Management → Create lifecycle rule
starter_state.current_configuration: All logs currently sit in S3 Standard indefinitely, with no lifecycle policy applied

requirements: Keep logs in S3 Standard for the first 7 days (active debugging period)
Transition to S3 Standard-IA at day 7 (occasional lookups still need reasonably fast access)
Transition to Glacier Deep Archive at day 90 (audit-only retention)
Expire (delete) the logs at day 365, matching the 1-year audit requirement
hints: Active debugging window-க்கு, S3 Standard-ஐ முதல் few days-க்கு அப்படியே வெச்சுக்கோ - transition rule 7 நாள் delay-ஆ start ஆகணும்
Deep Archive-க்கு direct-ஆ 90 நாள்-ல move பண்ணலாம் - Glacier Flexible Retrieval இதுக்கு தேவை இல்ல, ஏன்னா audit-only access, retrieval speed critical இல்ல
Expiration date, retention requirement-கூட exactly match ஆகணும் - அதிகமா வெச்சிருந்தா unnecessary cost, குறைவா வெச்சிருந்தா compliance violation

expected_outcome.verifiable_result: A lifecycle policy with transitions at day 7 (to Standard-IA) and day 90 (to Glacier Deep Archive), and expiration at day 365
expected_outcome.ava_correct: Correct! இந்த policy, access pattern-ஐ accurately reflect பண்ணுது - active period fast access, archive period cheap storage, retention period exact-ஆ compliance-ஐ match பண்ணுது.
expected_outcome.ava_wrong: Transition days-ஐ ஒரு தடவை check பண்ணு - active debugging window-க்கு பிறகு தான் Standard-IA-க்கு move ஆகணும், அப்புறம் archive access pattern ஆரம்பிச்சதும் Deep Archive-க்கு move ஆகணும்.

blocks.block_title: Product Images Accidentally Archived to Glacier
blocks.ava_speaks: ananya-analyst, cost optimization பண்ணும்போது, ஒரு overly broad lifecycle rule apply பண்ணிட்டாங்க - 'foodquick-product-images-prod' bucket முழுசும், 90 நாள் கழிச்சு Glacier-க்கு transition ஆகணும்னு set பண்ணி. ஆனா இந்த bucket-ல, actively-served menu item photos-மும் இருந்துச்சு.
blocks.setup: ananya-analyst, aiming to reduce S3 costs across the board, applies a bucket-wide lifecycle rule to foodquick-product-images-prod that transitions all objects to Glacier after 90 days, without checking whether every object in that bucket is genuinely archival.
blocks.what_happened: Menu item photos older than 90 days — many of which are still actively displayed on the FoodQuick app for long-standing restaurant menu items — get transitioned to Glacier. When the app tries to load these images, it can't retrieve them instantly; users see broken image placeholders instead of menu photos.
blocks.broken_config:
Lifecycle rule: transition-to-glacier-90-days
Scope: entire foodquick-product-images-prod bucket (no exclusion for actively-served content)
Transition: 90 days -> Glacier Flexible Retrieval (retrieval takes minutes to hours)

Application behavior: expects synchronous, millisecond image loads for the product catalog — completely incompatible with Glacier's retrieval model
blocks.error_shown: Application error logs: Image load failed for menu-items/pizza-margherita.jpg — S3 GetObject returned InvalidObjectState: The operation is not valid for the object's storage class. Frontend displays broken image icon.
blocks.the_real_problem: Lifecycle rule bucket-ஓட முழு content-ஐயும், ஒரே access pattern வெச்சிருக்குனு assume பண்ணுச்சு. ஆனா real-ஆ, அந்த bucket-ல ரெண்டு completely different access patterns கலந்திருந்துச்சு - சில genuinely old, unused images, சில actively-served, currently-displayed images. Glacier-ல இருந்து synchronous, immediate retrieval சாத்தியமே இல்ல - அதனால இது ஒரு silent, gradual application breakage-ஆ தெரிஞ்சுது.

fix.corrected_config:
1. Immediately restore the actively-served images out of Glacier back to S3 Standard (this requires an explicit restore request and a wait time).
2. Redesign the lifecycle rule with a filter/prefix that ONLY targets genuinely inactive content (e.g. only images for restaurants marked 'permanently closed'), not the entire bucket indiscriminately.
3. Consider S3 Intelligent-Tiering instead for this bucket, which automatically moves objects between tiers based on actual observed access patterns, rather than a blind time-based rule.
fix.result: Actively-served images are restored to fast-access storage, and the lifecycle rule now correctly targets only genuinely archival content going forward.

blocks.lesson: Lifecycle rules bucket-wide-ஆ, content-ஓட actual access pattern-ஐ கவனிக்காம apply பண்றது, actively-used content-ஐயும் தப்பா archive பண்ணி, application breakage-க்கு வழிவகுக்கும் - archival policies-ஐ, genuinely archival content-க்கு மட்டும் scope பண்ணணும்.

challenges.question: A dataset's access pattern is unpredictable and hard to characterize in advance — sometimes accessed daily for weeks, then not touched for months, with no clear schedule. What storage approach handles this without manual guesswork?
challenges.answer: S3 Intelligent-Tiering — it automatically monitors actual access patterns and moves objects between tiers based on real usage, rather than requiring someone to predict and hardcode a time-based lifecycle schedule that might not match reality.

challenges.question: A team applies a lifecycle rule transitioning objects to Glacier at 30 days, but doesn't realize their application periodically re-reads ALL objects in the bucket (including old ones) for a monthly reconciliation job. What's the risk?
challenges.answer: The reconciliation job will fail or hang when it hits objects in Glacier, since those require an explicit restore request and a wait time before they're readable again — the job's assumption of uniform, immediate access across all objects breaks the moment some of them archive.

challenges.question: A compliance team requires that certain financial records be retrievable within 24 hours if requested by an auditor, but otherwise are almost never accessed. Between Glacier Flexible Retrieval (minutes-hours) and Deep Archive (12+ hours), which better fits a strict same-day requirement?
challenges.answer: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is the safer fit — Deep Archive's 12+ hour retrieval time leaves very little margin if an audit request comes in later in the day, while Flexible Retrieval's minutes-to-hours window comfortably meets a 24-hour requirement with room to spare.

blocks.block_title: How Teams Avoid Bucket-Wide Lifecycle Mistakes
blocks.ava_speaks: Real companies-ல, lifecycle policies apply பண்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி, bucket-ஓட content-ஐ carefully categorize பண்றது ஒரு standard practice.

workflow_steps.action: Separate genuinely archival content from actively-served content into different buckets or prefixes before applying any lifecycle rule
workflow_steps.detail: இது ananya-analyst-ஓட mistake மாதிரி, ஒரே bucket-ல mixed access patterns-ஐ blind-ஆ ஒரே rule-ல treat பண்றதை தடுக்கும்

workflow_steps.action: Test a new lifecycle rule on a small subset or a non-production bucket first, observing the actual transition behavior before applying broadly
workflow_steps.detail: இது unexpected application breakage-ஐ, production-ல impact ஆவதுக்கு முன்னாடியே கண்டுபிடிக்க உதவும்

workflow_steps.action: Use S3 Storage Lens or S3 Analytics to understand actual access patterns across a bucket before designing lifecycle rules based on assumptions
workflow_steps.detail: Data-driven decisions, guesswork-ஐ விட ரொம்ப reliable-ஆ இருக்கும்

tools_shown.use: Bucket-level storage usage மற்றும் activity metrics-ஐ organization-wide-ஆ காட்டி, cost optimization opportunities மற்றும் risky patterns identify பண்ண உதவும்
Access patterns unpredictable-ஆ இருக்கும்போது, manual lifecycle rules-க்கு பதிலா, automatic, usage-based tier movement தரும்

lesson_summary.ava_speaks: Nalla progress! இன்னைக்கு நாம S3 Standard, Standard-IA, Glacier, Deep Archive trade-offs, lifecycle policies எப்படி automatic transitions பண்ணும்னு கத்துக்கிட்டோம். மிக முக்கியமா, actively-served content-ஐ archival storage class-க்கு தப்பா move பண்றது, application breakage-க்கு வழிவகுக்கும்னு உறுதியா கத்துக்கிட்ட. அடுத்த lesson-ல நாம S3 Security பார்ப்போம் - Block Public Access, bucket policies, encryption.

board.title: Lesson C5.1b — Summary
points: ✓ S3 Standard, Standard-IA, Glacier, and Deep Archive trade storage cost against retrieval cost and retrieval time
✓ Cheaper storage always comes with either a retrieval fee, a retrieval delay, or both
✓ Lifecycle policies automate storage class transitions based on object age, avoiding manual file management
✓ S3 Intelligent-Tiering handles unpredictable access patterns better than a fixed time-based lifecycle rule
✓ A bucket-wide lifecycle rule that doesn't account for actively-served content can silently break an application
